column1: # Axis A: the option leaves whose canonical magnitude names nothing, and what
# a hit looks like for them.
# This is the same mechanism `axis-d-observables.tsv` declares for a root
# outside `rules:`, applied where the round measured it to be needed on axis A.
# The three framework keys are not read through `fromArray()`: the factory
# drains them into the registry's providers, and the stand observes them by
# asking the predicates themselves — `isPathExcluded('src/Sub/Helper.php')` and
# `isNamespaceExcluded('Probe\Sub')`. A canonical `[7331]` names neither, so
# the probe changes nothing, so `omitted == equivalent` and every one of the
# row's eight cells reads NOT OBSERVABLE for a reason that belongs to the
# stand.
# The hit replaces the MAGNITUDE of the reference form's write; its shape is
# unchanged. It is used for the `equivalent` side AND for the cell of that same
# form — a hit on `equivalent` alone would leave the form's own cell writing a
# magnitude that names nothing, and the stand would then read the correct
# behaviour "accepted a list of a path that is not here, changed nothing" as
# the INERT defect. That asymmetry is a measured defect of the axis-D code and
# is corrected in the same place.
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated rather than left to be discovered: the other
# seven forms of a hit-carrying row still write 7331. `suppress-paths: 7331`
# reading INERT cannot be split by this stand into "the int form was accepted
# and dropped" and "the int form was coerced into a path that names nothing".
# The row is the form of the container (README, "What the oracle does not
# prove"), and that limit is unchanged here.
option_leaf
column3: why the canonical write cannot hit
